annotations.text:
The tank pass — 16 September.

Two references. crechetank.com gave us staging, voice and material: a mono third type voice for kickers, hints and Rascal; one pane of frosted glass (the sheet, and only the sheet — the map ghosts through at every detent); Rascal talking in blob bubbles; the critter in front of the display title on Saved; heads floating in a room for the picker and for People; grain and a vignette on the map.

Corner gave us features: friends' one-line takes on a place (vibe checks), searching your own Stash, category chips that compose with the person chips, and the saver's note on detail.

Rejected on purpose: coral display type (titles stay ink), gloss (Rascal stays matte), whole-scene blur, a serif, ranks and streaks, dense labelled pins.

Water is the only colour that came from the tank. By day it is the lake; at dusk it is the tank at night.

Every kicker on page 1 is now mono too — one change to kicker() in parts-a.mjs restyled the whole set.

Still to render: rascal-sniff.png and rascal-cheer.png off the same rig. Both boards use the peek pose as a stand-in.

Dusk is a token swap over finished boards (toDusk), not a second design system. Nothing in the app consumes it yet.

Places — three detents.

The middle artboard is live: drag or tap the handle to move between peek, half and full; tap a chip to filter; tap a pin or a row and the other side follows. Drag the map to pan, +/- to zoom, arrow to recentre.

The sheet stops at the top of the tab bar rather than running underneath it — that overlap is what was swallowing the peek state. Detents are measured against the 761pt tab-screen height, not the full 844.

Rascal peeks over the sheet at peek and ducks away as it opens. Filter to one person and their pins gain that member's critter while everyone else's collapse to 14px dots.

The save loop, end to end.

Confirm is live: it opens on Rascal sniffing, lands on the high-confidence result, and "not right" opens the other two. "None of these" drops into search with the city pre-filled. Add to Stash runs a mock save into the success moment.

Add-a-place takes a pasted link, a search, or typed details — three sources, so the app never reads as a single-source client.

Place detail is where "I'm in" lives, and the only route out to the original post.

Third tab is People, not Den.

A Den is an object a person can have several of, so it can't be the destination — People is the column, and this Den is what's inside it.

Onboarding keeps what it collects: a name beside the critter, a name and emblem for the Den. Both steps currently throw the answer away.

E is the recommendation.

Adding a place is a global verb — you do it because you saw a reel, not because of what is on screen. Global verbs want a stable home, and the corner is the only spot that is screen-anchored, thumb-reachable, and free at all three detents.

So position never changes; only the form does. Labelled while the map is dominant and there is room, a bare circle once the list needs the space. That keeps A's teaching value without A's moving target.

Rascal keeps the sheet edge above it — different band, no collision.

Where does the + live?

Adding a place is the whole product, so this is worth getting right rather than parking it at the end of the chip row where it is now.

A · Docked on the sheet. A labelled pill while the map is dominant, collapsing to a circle as the sheet rises — the label earns its place only when there is room. Thumb-reachable, and it choreographs with Rascal. Costs the most motion, and it moves, so it is never in one remembered spot.

B · Header action. Always in the same place, unmissable next to the title, and it absorbs the search icon which already opened the same sheet. Worst thumb reach on a large phone, and it competes with the screen title.

C · Fixed corner. The convention, and the most predictable: one place, always, at every detent. Reads generic, and it sits on top of a row at the taller detents.

D · Raised in the nav. Loudest possible signal that this is the main action. But it puts a global verb in a bar reserved for destinations, and §7 fixed that bar at three.

E · Fixed corner, morphing form. C's stable home with A's prominence, carried by size and label rather than by position. The pill collapses to a circle as the sheet rises.

The critter roster is now urban.

Raccoon, possum, squirrel, skunk — the animals that actually raid a city at night. That settles the tension in §10.4 at the roster level: cozy low-poly read pastoral when the cast was fox, owl and frog.

The four heads share one rig — same dodecagon skull, same facet breaks, same eye and snout construction — so a new critter is markings and a palette, which is the half-hour claim in §10.5.

Rascal is the supplied render. The critters are vector stand-ins and want renders from the same rig.
